string.text: You prepare to set off for a grand adventure in Calradia! Here is your character. Continue if you are ready, or go back to make changes.
You were born into a family of...
Better to be a warrior in a garden than a gardener in a war.
A healthy mind in a healthy body.
Necessity is the mother of invention.
To conquer without risk is to triumph without glory.
The temptation of travel was to much for you, as you always dreamt of seeing the world.
After being wronged, you felt the need for revenge. With that goal in mind, you wandered throughout Calradia to get reparations.
After one last disagreement with you, your parents forced you out. With nowhere to go, adventuring was all you could do.
You always wanted to make riches, and it was obvious for you that staying at home would never allow you to do it.
to become one of the powerful
Seeing how those in power had many advantages, you joined on an adventure to join them, or even replace them.
With all the wars in Calradia, there are many way one could carve {?PLAYER.GENDER}her{?}his{\?} name in history.
after the loss of a loved one
After losing some close to you, you left to see if you could fill that hole
Your craftmanship has been an important part of your life, but your skill wasn't enough. You thus decided to embark on a journey to improve at it.
Having been taught in medicine, you decide to set out and help those in need, as with the wars many have suffered.
Attaching much importance to your fighting skill, you figured there was no better place than calradia to prove your might.
Your character started off on the adventuring path at the age of...
While lacking experience a bit, you are full with youthful energy, you are fully eager, for the long years of adventuring ahead.
You are at your prime, You still have some youthful energy but also have a substantial amount of experience under your belt.
This is the right age for starting off, you have years of experience, and you are old enough for people to respect you and gather under your banner.
While you are past your prime, there is still enough time to go on that last big adventure for you. And you have all the experience you need to overcome anything!

Burning Empires stopped loading this campaign because its custom data could not be migrated safely.
What happened: The save declares data version {SOURCE_VERSION}, while this build requires version {TARGET_VERSION}. The continuous module migration chain or its validation failed.
Technical reason: {REASON}
What the program did: No population, religion, relation, reputation, Wonder, Historical Campaign, or custom-value data was committed to the running campaign. The original .sav and its external snapshots were not modified.
What to do: Keep the original save and the matching BESavedata campaign directory together. Restore a Burning Empires build that supports this source version, or add the missing continuous module migration and validation step before trying again.
This save slot was previously deleted through Bannerlord's saved-games screen. Burning Empires has ignored the old embedded recovery reference so that deleted external data cannot recreate itself.

This v{0} save has a damaged active external snapshot, but Burning Empires found a valid backup from the same physical save slot. It will restore that backup and migrate a deep copy to v{1}; the original files will not be overwritten.

Technical reason:
External save data could not be fully deleted

Burning Empires blocked {OPERATION} because this session contains data migrated from an older save.
Why this happened: The original old-version save is being preserved as a rollback point. Ordinary saving is disabled until the required migration Save As has succeeded.
What to do: Close this message and use the migration prompt to enter a new, unique save name. After that Save As succeeds, all normal save commands and branch-specific automatic saves become available again.

Bannerlord deleted the selected .sav file, but Burning Empires could not read its UniqueGameId from the save metadata.
What happened: The external data folder is keyed by both Campaign ID and save-slot name. A slot name alone is not sufficient because two different campaigns can use the same name.
Affected save slot: {SAVE_NAME}
What the program did: Burning Empires preserved all external data instead of guessing which campaign directory should be removed. No other save was changed.
What to do: Close the game and inspect BESavedata/campaigns only if you need to remove the unmatched external slot manually. Do not delete another campaign directory merely because it contains a slot with the same name.

Burning Empires disabled branch-specific automatic saves for this game session.
What happened: The version-locked autosave hook or save-list UI contract is missing, failed, or conflicts with another Mod. Running both implementations could overwrite another save branch, invoke Bannerlord's save callback twice, or build an invalid save list.
Technical detail: {REASON}
What the program did: No fallback to the global saveauto1-3 slots was attempted. If the conflict affects SavedGameGroup, the BE branch hierarchy is also disabled and the original flat save list is retained. Manual Save, Quick Save, Save As, Save and Exit, and loading remain available.
What to do: Keep this report, compare the listed Harmony or UIExtenderEx owner with the enabled module list, and disable or update the Mod that changes the same save method or SavedGameGroup prefab. Restart Bannerlord after changing the module list.

This campaign was loaded from Burning Empires data version {SOURCE_VERSION} and has been migrated to version {TARGET_VERSION}.
What this means: The migrated data is currently held only in memory. Burning Empires will not overwrite the old save. You must create a new save slot before Quick Save, Auto Save, Save, or Save and Exit can be used.
Migrated modules: {MODULES}
What to do: Enter a new, unique save name below and select Save migrated campaign. The new slot remains part of the same Bannerlord campaign, but receives its own Burning Empires save-branch identity and its own three automatic-save slots.
The migrated Burning Empires campaign has been saved to its new slot.
The migrated campaign was not saved

Bannerlord could not finish the required Save As operation.
What happened: The migrated Burning Empires data remains only in memory, so ordinary saves are still blocked to protect the original old-version save.
What to do: Check that the save folder is writable and that sufficient disk space is available. Close this message, then enter a different new save name when the migration prompt appears again.
Enter a name for the migrated save.
The save name must contain fewer than 30 characters.

This is a Historical Campaign character-selection playerEquipment configuration error.
What this means: The game could not find one or more preview items or equipment rosters configured for {CHARACTER_NAME} ({HERO_ID}) in BE ModuleData Source Files/BEData/be_historical_campaign.json.
Why it happened: An itemId or equipmentRosterId does not exist, is misspelled, or was not loaded into the current ModuleData. The selection tableau uses a safe visual fallback, but starting the campaign is blocked until playerEquipment is valid because the chosen Hero must receive the exact JSON battle equipment.
What the program did: Only the temporary preview used a fallback. No real Hero equipment was modified.
Configuration details: {ISSUES}
How to fix it: Open BE ModuleData Source Files/BEData/be_historical_campaign.json, correct the listed playerEquipment field, slot, or object ID, then run BE ModuleData Builder/BEModuleDataBuilder.exe validate, dry-run, and pack in that order. Reopen Historical Campaign and verify the preview.
Historical Campaign preview equipment configuration needs attention

Historical Campaign could not enable the mouse-wheel zoom and middle-button vertical camera controls for the character preview.
What this is: The character model itself is still available, but the small compatibility bridge that changes the real three-dimensional Tableau camera position could not connect to Bannerlord's CharacterTableau fields.
Why it happened: This build expects the Bannerlord 1.4.7 CharacterTableau structure. A different game version or an incompatible UI assembly can rename or replace the required private fields. Technical detail: {TECHNICAL_REASON}
What the program did: Mouse-wheel zoom and middle-button vertical camera movement have been disabled for this session to prevent an unsafe reflection write. Character selection, left-button rotation, and Begin Campaign remain available.
What to do: Confirm that Bannerlord 1.4.7 and the required official prerequisite modules are installed. If the versions are correct, send this complete message and the Historical Campaign log to mumahutuo so the compatibility bridge can be updated. Do not edit be_historical_campaign.json for this error.
Historical Campaign preview camera compatibility error

Burning Empires could not safely finish loading this Historical Campaign save.
What happened: {REASON}
Why this check exists: Bannerlord reloads the Sandbox-only main_hero, player_faction and main_hero_party_template XML definitions while reading a save. A valid Historical Campaign save uses the selected historical Hero and Clan instead. The unused Sandbox definitions may be removed only when they own no assets and have no active references.
What the program did: Loading of Wonder stash inventories, discovery state and the remaining Burning Empires external data was stopped before those values could be applied to an unsafe world state. No placeholder Hero was killed and no Clan-destruction or asset-transfer action was used.
What to do: Do not overwrite this save. Keep the save file and the complete BurningEmpires Logs directory, then report candidate ID {CANDIDATE_ID} and the message above to the Burning Empires programmer. Test again with a save created by the current DLL after the reported reference has been corrected.
